subject: Post-call: FinCap data-handling & oncall break-glass playbook
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@fincap.com>, Aaron Miller <aaron.miller@fincap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinCap data-handling & oncall break-glass playbook

Thanks for taking the time today — helpful call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on data handling expectations and support access for FinCap production workloads.

Summary from our call:
- Scope: FinCap will run anonymized customer analytics + occasional PII-enriched support traces (credit card last4, masked SSN) for fraud investigations. No full PAN storage.
- Residency: Primary production region US-east, possibility of EU region for limited datasets later.
- Retention: Transaction-level telemetry retained 90 days by default; investigation artifacts may be retained up to 7 years (regulated).
- Logging & audit: Need per-request audit logs, per-token tracing disabled for PII, and retention of access logs for minimum 1 year.
- Support access model: RBAC + ephemeral break-glass for emergency support; customer-managed approval workflow required for any elevated session.

Attachments I shared: redwood-data-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook draft), SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx (evidence we can provide).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Sandra/Aaron: confirm if FinCap requires HSM-backed KMS for encryption at rest or if cloud KMS is acceptable (answer by Fri 7/9).
2) Marissa/Vivek: please draft a concise break-glass runbook (1–2 pages) that maps roles, approval steps, and evidence capture requirements — target EOD Thu 7/8.
3) I'll schedule a focused 30-min follow-up to walk the playbook and handshake on SLA/response times. Proposed slot: Mon 7/12 11:00am ET (I’ll send invite).

Thanks — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
[attachment: redwood-data-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF)]
[attachment: SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@fincap.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Miller <aaron.miller@fincap.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCap data-handling & oncall break-glass playbook

Vanessa — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick answers from our side: 
- KMS: We prefer HSM-backed KMS for keys that decrypt any PII; cloud KMS acceptable only if HSM option unavailable. Procurement will confirm options but treat as HSM requirement for now.
- Residency: US-east primary is fine; will flag EU as possible future requirement for specific customer cohorts.
- Retention: Investigation artifacts retained 7 years is necessary for compliance.
- Break-glass: We require MFA-backed approvals and an explicit audit bundle for each elevated session (who/why/TTL/screenshot of approval) retained for 3 years.

A couple of asks from procurement: can Redwood provide a sample SOC2 report redacted for other customers, and a short note on data deletion/ERASURE workflow? If you can attach a redacted SOC2 and a 1-page erasure summary that helps accelerate procurement.

Will also loop Legal if we need to add tighter language into the contract.

Best,
Sandra
Director, Platform Security — FinCap
[sandra.lopez@fincap.com | +1 (212) 555-0198]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCap data-handling & oncall break-glass playbook

Looping in Vivek for runtime/ops input. I’ll take ownership of the break-glass runbook draft. Initial checklist I’ll cover: 
- Roles & least-privilege mappings (SupportEngineer, InfraOncall, CustomerAdmin)
- MFA + OOB approval flow (slack -> idp approval -> temporary RBAC elevation)
- TTLs (default 15m, escalatable to 4h with exec approval)
- Evidence capture: session recording metadata, request IDs, approval artifacts stored in audit store for 3 yrs
- Safeguards: KV cache scrub for any access that could surface PII, token redaction policy, auto-revoke on idle

Vivek — can you confirm whether our current audit-store supports 3-year retention for session bundles and whether HSM-backed KMS is in our supported deployment options for Redwood Private? If not, what timeline for offering it?

I’ll circulate the 2-page draft by EOD Thu so Vanessa can share with FinCap.

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@fincap.com>, Aaron Miller <aaron.miller@fincap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCap data-handling & oncall break-glass playbook

Sandra/Aaron — thanks for the clarifications, noted on HSM preference and retention windows. Action items we’ll follow through on this week: 
- Marissa: break-glass runbook (EOD Thu 7/8) — will include MFA approval flow and evidence bundle template.
- Vivek: confirm audit-store retention & HSM/private deploy options (ETA: Tue 7/13).
- Vanessa: provide redacted SOC2 and a 1-page data erasure workflow (attached).

I’ve attached a one-page erasure summary and the playbook draft (internal) so you can see the shape of the runbook. If these look good, propose a quick 30-min call Mon 7/12 11:00am ET to finalize SLA language for the contract.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to procurement/Legal.

Vanessa
